correctness.rationale: With complete spatial absorption and independent uniform starting position and angle, the killed resolvent is paired against the same constant on both sides. The symmetric Dirichlet operator A_q has a gap q+D lambda_1 even for D_R=0. The form estimate gives ||B A_q^(-1/2)||<=D^(-1/2); integrating by parts with zero spatial trace gives K=A_q^(-1/2) B A_q^(-1/2) bounded and skew-adjoint without requiring tangential propulsion. The factorization can be made on the form space, which A_q^(-1/2) maps onto. At q=0 the time integral is finite: in any unit interval a translational Brownian displacement larger than diam(G)+v guarantees exit regardless of the heading path and uniformly over surviving initial data, yielding a geometric upper bound on the tail at integer times. Averaging the two adjoint resolvents gives (I+v^2 K*K)^(-1) in the constant-vector pairing. For the crucial zero-atom check, Kf=0 implies the spatial directional derivative of A_q^(-1/2)f vanishes in G for almost every heading. Extend each spatial section by zero; the extension is H^1, so its directional derivative vanishes on the whole plane. Almost every parallel line then carries a constant square-integrable section, hence zero. This proves injectivity, including frozen headings. The spectral formula yields strict alternating derivatives and strict pairwise order, dominated convergence gives the high-speed limit, and Cauchy–Schwarz and Jensen give the reciprocal concavity and stated tangent rational bound. At q=0 the comparison is of means; only q>0 yields a strict comparison of exit-time Laplace transforms. Read 'both averages are essential' as the stated release hypothesis, not a universal necessity: for D_R=0 the same spatial argument works at each fixed heading with uniform position. No fixed-start or pointwise survival ordering is implied. The supplied finite matrix and one-dimensional normalization checks were inspected, not executed; they do not validate the planar kernel argument or the infinite hierarchy.

value.rationale: The model is a standard first-passage problem where fixed-start effects and weak-activity coefficients do not settle the direction of a uniform-release comparison. The strict ordering of every discounted observable at any two speeds and the explicit bounded spectral representation provide useful constraints without fitting a shape-specific propagator or claiming pointwise time order. The absence of a zero atom is mathematically consequential and gives high-speed vanishing rather than only the passive upper bound.
